paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu believed that the most important question was how the people of Kai and Shinano regarded Nobunaga's death. Since both lands had for generations been domains of the Kai Genji, the people naturally had not welcomed Nobunaga's harsh policies; but just how deep did their resentment run? Only by clearly grasping the people's true response could he make the right decision.

paragraphs.source_en: Ieyasu had first extended his feelers toward Kōfu on the seventh day of the sixth month, six days after Nobunaga's death and after Ieyasu's desperate flight from the port of Sakai back to Okazaki. The two men he dispatched were Honda Hyakusuke Nobutoshi and Nagura Kihachirō Nobumitsu. Ostensibly, their mission was to pay their respects to Kawajiri Hizen-no-kami Hidetaka, the castellan of Kōfu.
